extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients, institutional grants administrators, PD/PIs, and Authorized Organization Representatives (AORs)
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative policies and prior-approval criteria governing NIH grant administration, including carryover of unobligated balances, no-cost extensions, rebudgeting, changes in scope or personnel, transfers of awards, and documentation required for prior-approval requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic carryover applicability and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic carryover of unobligated balances applies to all awards except centers (P50, P60, P30, other), cooperative agreements (U), Kirschstein-NRSA institutional research training grants (T), non-Fast Track Phase I SBIR and STTR awards (R43 and R41), clinical trials (regardless of activity code), and awards to individuals. Other awards may be excluded through a specific term or condition in the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For excluded awards, carryover of unobligated balances requires NIH awarding IC prior approval unless otherwise noted in the NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP automatic carryover and reporting >25% requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards under SNAP, funds are automatically carried over to the subsequent budget period. The recipient must indicate in the progress report whether any estimated unobligated balance (including prior-year carryover) is expected to be greater than 25 percent of the current year’s total approved budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the unobligated balance is greater than 25 percent of the total approved budget, the recipient must provide an explanation and indicate plans for expenditure of those funds within the current budget year. Total approved budget includes current year and any carryover from prior years of the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFR reporting of carryover when annual FFR required
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards that require an annual FFR, the amount to be carried over must be specified under item 12, 'Remarks.'

rubrics_metrics.name: GMO review and potential actions for >25% unobligated balances
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient reports a balance of unobligated funds in excess of 25 percent of the total amount awarded for the budget period plus any approved carryover, the GMO will review the circumstances to ensure funds are necessary to complete the project and may request additional information, including a revised budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some or all unobligated funds are not necessary, the GMO may restrict future automatic carryover authority, use the balance to reduce or offset NIH funding for a subsequent budget period, or combine these actions; the decision will be reflected in the NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year cancellation and FFR disbursement deadline (31 U.S.C. §1552(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All Federal agencies must close fixed year appropriation accounts and cancel remaining balances by September 30 of the fifth fiscal year after the year of availability. Recipients must report disbursements on the FFR no later than August 31 of the fifth fiscal year after the year of availability; at the end of five years funds are cancelled and returned to the Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory provision may limit the availability of funds for carryover or authority to extend final budget periods when an entire project period is funded by a single award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-related prior approvals (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH prior approval is not required to rebudget funds for any direct cost item that the applicable cost principles identify as requiring the Federal awarding agency’s prior approval, unless the incurrence of costs is associated with or is considered to be a change in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time extension of final budget period without additional NIH funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient may extend the final budget period of the previously approved project period one time for up to 12 months beyond the original completion date if: no term of award specifically prohibits the extension; no additional funds are required; and the project’s originally approved scope will not change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must use the eRA Commons No-Cost Extension feature (available 90 days before project end) to notify NIH electronically. Notifications may not be submitted via e-mail or fax. Late notifications convert to a request requiring IC GMO approval. Recipients must update required certifications and assurances for the extension period. The provision does not apply to fellowship awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct charging administrative and clerical salaries — four conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries of administrative and clerical staff should normally be treated as indirect costs. Direct charging is appropriate only if all of the following are met: (1) administrative or clerical services are integral to a project or activity; (2) individuals involved can be specifically identified with the project or activity; (3) such costs are explicitly included in the budget; and (4) the costs are not also recovered as indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such charges must also meet the criteria for allowable costs in 2 CFR Part 200.403. NIH prior approval is not required to rebudget funds for this direct cost item post-award, but prior approval is required when additional funds are being requested for such a position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental compensation under written institutional policy for IHEs
rubrics_metrics.description: IHEs may direct charge payments of incidental activities for which supplemental compensation is allowable under written institutional policy (at a rate not to exceed the institutional base salary) and not include them in the records described in 2 CFR Part 200.430.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such activities must be specifically provided for in the Federal award budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-IHE faculty consulting exceeding base salary — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: IHEs may include charges for intra-IHE faculty consulting on sponsored agreements that exceed a faculty member’s base salary only in unusual cases where: (a) consultation is across departmental lines or involves a separate or remote operation; and (b) the consulting work is in addition to the faculty member’s regular departmental load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit 7 — Prior approval required: additional no-cost extension or extension >12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH prior approval is required for additional no-cost extensions, extensions greater than 12 months, or late notification of an initial no-cost extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All instances require prior approval per Exhibit 7; see 8.1.2.1 for request content and limitations (including statutory five-year closure considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit 7 — Prior approval required: Alterations & Renovations (A&R)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH prior approval is required for rebudgeting into A&R costs that would exceed 25 percent of the total approved budget for a budget period; also required for lesser rebudgeting into A&R if the rebudgeting would result in a change in scope or if addition of a Major A&R project occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rebudgeting results in addition of a Major A&R project, NIH will consider it a change in scope and will apply documentation requirements (see Construction Grants chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit 7 — Prior approval required: capital expenditures and encumbering real property
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital expenditures (construction, land, or building acquisition) require NIH prior approval. Any proposals to convey, transfer, assign, mortgage, lease, or otherwise encumber real property acquired with NIH grant funds also require prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit 7 — Prior approval required: carryover of unobligated balances when NoA limits authority
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH prior approval is required for carryover of unobligated balances if the NoA indicates the recipient does not have automatic carryover authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prior approval is required, the AOR should submit a request to the GMO with specified minimum documentation (detailed budget with indirect cost info, scientific justification for use of funds, and reason for the unobligated balance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover prior-approval request required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: When NIH prior approval for carryover is required, the request must include at minimum: a detailed budget by direct cost category with indirect cost information (base and rate); a scientific justification for the use of funds; and the reason for the unobligated balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect rate used to approve carryover generally will be the rate in effect at the time the initial funds were awarded for the year to which the funds are being carried over; actual expenditures are based on the rate applicable when cost is incurred. If personnel costs are requested, include detailed breakdown (base salary, salary requested, effort).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in scope — definition and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in scope is a change in the direction, aims, objectives, purposes, or type of research training identified in the approved project; the recipient must obtain prior approval for a change in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential indicators include but are not limited to: change in specific aims, substitution of animal model, change from non-human to human subjects, change from exempt to non-exempt human subjects research, change from 'No Clinical Trial' to 'Includes a Clinical Trial' (such changes must be submitted to a clinical trial NOFO as a competitive revision), inclusion of populations covered by additional protections (45 CFR 46 subparts B/C/D), any protocol change increasing risk to subjects, new information indicating higher risk, shift of research emphasis to another disease area, FDA clinical hold under an IND/IDE, application of a new technology (e.g., new assays), transfer of substantive programmatic work to a third party (especially foreign components), change in other senior/key personnel not named in the NoA, significant rebudgeting (see definition), incurrence of research patient care costs not previously approved, and purchase of equipment > $25,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant rebudgeting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant rebudgeting occurs when expenditures in a single direct cost budget category deviate (increase or decrease) from the categorical commitment level established for the budget period by 25 percent or more of the total costs awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if award total costs are $200,000, any rebudgeting that results in an increase or decrease of more than $50,000 in a budget category is significant. Base excludes prior-year carryover but includes competing and non-competing supplements. Significant rebudgeting does not apply to modular grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in status of PD/PI and senior/key personnel — prior approval thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must submit a prior approval request if there is a significant change in status of the PD/PI or other Senior/Key Personnel named in the NoA including withdrawal from the project; absence for any continuous period of 3 months or more; or reduction of time or effort by 25 percent or more (cumulative) from approved level. Also requires approval for change between multiple PD/PI and single PD/PI models and changes in number/makeup of PD/PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting 'Yes' in the RPPR constitutes a prior approval request and issuance of a subsequent year of funding constitutes approval. NIH must approve any alternate arrangements or replacements. Requests must include strong scientific justification, biographical sketch of proposed individuals, other sources of support, and budget changes. A new/revised Leadership Plan is required if changing PD/PI model. Commons ID is required for new PD/PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety/work environment disclosure and notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to change or replace PD/PI or senior/key personnel should include mention whether changes are related to concerns about safety and/or work environments (bullying, retaliation, or hostile working conditions). Recipient institutions are required to notify NIH when individuals identified as PD/PI or Senior/Key Personnel are removed or disciplined due to such concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be provided by the AOR within 30 days via the dedicated web form and include at minimum: name of AOR, name of individual of concern, description of concerns, actions taken, and any anticipated impact on NIH-funded award(s). NIH may require prior approval for replacement and may decline transfer of awards if concerns are unresolved. NIH has authority to share investigation reports and requires institutions to complete investigations to continue receiving NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient organization — prior approval and permissive conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH prior approval is required for transfer of legal and administrative responsibility for a grant-supported project from one legal entity to another before completion of the approved project period. A change may be permitted if the original recipient agrees to relinquish responsibility before completion, or if a non-competing continuation award has been withheld because of recipient actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grant to an individual may not be transferred. A successor-in-interest or name change is not a change of recipient. Transfers involving foreign organizations or international organizations must be approved by the IC’s Advisory Council. NIH will consider whether permanent benefits, facilities/resources, time remaining, and percentage of funds allow successful performance; peer review may be required if conditions are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient organization — timing and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A change of recipient request must be made before the anticipated start date at the new organization and preferably several months in advance. Failure to provide timely notification may result in disapproval or significant processing delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are encouraged to discuss potential issues with the awarding IC(s) prior to submission; for transfers mid-budget-period or at fiscal year end contact IC for guidance on timing and preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient organization — required application components (paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper application from the proposed new recipient organization should include at minimum: PHS 398 Face Page; Budget pages (current and future years) with modular guidance where applicable; Other Project Information and Senior/Key Personnel components; updated biographical sketches; progress report if transferring on anniversary date; updated other support pages if necessary; Resources page; Checklist page; Certification of IRB/IACUC approval (if applicable) including assurance numbers; detailed list of equipment purchased with grant funds to be transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets should not exceed the direct costs previously recommended for any budget period. For transfers in the middle of a budget period budget rules and modular guidance apply as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient organization — required application components (electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic application from the proposed recipient organization should include at minimum: SF 424 (R&R) Cover Component; SF 424 (R&R) Project Performance Site Location(s); SF 424 (R&R) Other Project Information including IRB/IACUC certifications and Facilities and Other Resources (probable effect of the move); detailed equipment list; SF 424 (R&R) Senior/Key Person Profile with updated biosketches and other support; budget pages applicable for activity code (current and future years); PHS 398 Research Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original award resulted from a modular application, electronic transfers should use the R&R Detailed Budget form and follow guidance for modular awards (either full fields or PD/PI costs plus other direct costs in Section F and indirect costs in Section H).
